title: Lattices of rings grow by bands, not by single rings
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: Every n x m torus of equally spaced rule-60 rings (n, m >= 3) has a half-turn at every contact exchanging its two rings, so every contact persists at every lag, and growth by inserting whole bands of rings round the torus or by splitting every ring into blocks keeps every contact persistent at every stage. Attaching a single new ring breaks persistence: by one contact (a return of length 1), by two contacts not side by side on one ring (an unpaired return of length 2), and as a bubble on a corner p -> q exactly when some contact is reached from q and reaches p.
